Insurance / EXPLAINER

How to compare insurance coverage fairly

Look past the premium to limits, exclusions, deductibles, and claims experience.

FH
FinancersHub editorial team
Editorial preview · Educational guide

Original editorial image for the FinancersHub design preview.

The cheapest premium is not always the least expensive outcome. Insurance comparisons make more sense when you hold coverage, exclusions, limits, and deductibles side by side.

KEEP IN MIND

Three questions to ask

  1. 01Are the coverage limits comparable?
  2. 02What deductibles and exclusions apply?
  3. 03Have your circumstances changed since the last review?

Compare the same protection

Ask each insurer for quotes with similar coverage types and limits. Review the deductible you would have to pay after a covered event and any separate deductible for a particular kind of claim. A lower premium may come with more cost at claim time.

Read the exclusions

The policy describes what is covered and what is not. Look for limits on valuable property, location-specific risks, and conditions that might affect a claim. If wording is unclear, ask the company or agent to explain it before purchase.

Review after a change

A move, new vehicle, renovation, or change in household can make an old policy a poor match. Keep a copy of your declarations and policy documents, and check the current terms at renewal rather than assuming coverage stayed the same.

SOURCE & FURTHER READING

Check the primary source

The guide is newly written for this preview and draws its factual background from National Association of Insurance Commissioners: Get smart about your insurance coverage ↗. Check that source and current product terms before making a decision.
